diagnosed: One real, reproducible mechanical breakage, unchanged since the 2026-11-06/07/09 runs and still the ONLY outstanding fault: the research ESCALATION fast-lane is 100% broken, and its only correct fix lives entirely in a protected path. Scout/coverage-critic request a deep escalation via scripts/escalate-research.js -> `gh workflow run research-agent.yml -f tier=deep` using the job GITHUB_TOKEN, so the dispatched run's actor is github-actions[bot] (type: Bot). anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 now rejects bot actors unless listed in allowed_bots, which no step sets — so every escalated deep-research run fails at its claude-code-action step with 'Action failed with error: Workflow initiated by non-human actor: github-actions (type: Bot). Add bot to allowed_bots list or use *'. Confirmed firsthand this run: run 42633516127 (2026-11-09T14:19Z, workflow_dispatch) failed BOTH the Fable 5 deep step and the Opus 4.8 deep-fallback step with that exact error, actor type logged as 'Bot'; the escalation path always passes -f tier=deep so only the two deep steps are exercised. Scheduled 4-hourly runs are human-actor (actor type 'User', verified CHaerem) and are unaffected — only the recall fast-lane is dead. The dispatch returns 200 so escalate-research.js reports success, making the failure invisible except as red research runs. Already tracked by OPEN issue #430 ('Research escalation fast-lane is 100% broken (bot actor rejected by claude-code-action)') with the complete, format-resolved recipe.

OWNER FIX NEEDED (protected .github/workflows/research-agent.yml) — ALREADY TRACKED by OPEN issue #430: add `allowed_bots: "github-actions"` (scope to the dispatching bot login, NOT `*` on a public repo — the action's isAllowedBot() strips the `[bot]` suffix and lowercases, so `github-actions` matches the github-actions[bot] actor) to the with: block of the claude-code-action@v1 steps. The escalation only ever dispatches -f tier=deep, so the two deep steps (Fable 5 'deep, preferred' ~line 98 and Opus 4.8 'deep fallback' ~line 127) are the ones that matter; adding it to the standard step too (~line 79) is harmless and uniform. Could NOT author the fix: this is the unattended Self-repair CI agent (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, CI=true, workflow 'Self-repair agent'), so the CI-only scripts/hooks/protect-automation.js PreToolUse hook fires and BLOCKS any Edit/Write/Bash mutation of .github/workflows/** ('A human must author changes to these files'). Re-confirmed this run: on branch self-repair/20261110-1535 the Edit adding allowed_bots to research-agent.yml was blocked by the hook (exit 2); branch deleted, working tree clean. By design, an unattended CI agent cannot author protected-path (.github/workflows/**) changes — so no PR is possible and the fix must be applied by a human.

No non-protected fix exists: the breakage is the bot-actor gate on the dispatched run. Any GITHUB_TOKEN-authenticated `gh workflow run`/repository_dispatch produces a Bot actor regardless of event, so changing escalate-research.js cannot make the dispatch a human actor without a new PAT secret and workflow wiring (itself a protected change). The one-line allowed_bots addition is the correct, minimal fix.
